findings.title: HSTS missing on https://jadawl.site (marketing domain) — the app at https://app.jadawl.site already passes (grade A, 90/100)
evidence: security-reports/raw/jadawl-site-headers.json: hsts -> None on jadawl.site (Bunny pull zone 6292730)
security-reports/raw/jadawl-app-headers.json: app.jadawl.site (pull zone 6480768) sends HSTS + Permissions-Policy correctly — the headers are stripped only on the marketing pull zone
findings.fix: For the marketing zone: verify origin sends HSTS after redeploy, then check Bunny passes it; if not, add an Edge Rule on zone 6292730 setting Strict-Transport-Security. Also set JADAWEL_ENABLE_SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER=yes in CranL env to enable Secure cookies and Django HSTS (documented in root Dockerfile comments).

findings.title: Permissions-Policy missing on jadawl.site (marketing domain only — app.jadawl.site passes)
evidence: jadawl-site-headers.json: permissions -> None on jadawl.site; jadawl-app-headers.json: app.jadawl.site sends it correctly
findings.fix: same path as SEC-HDR-001; if Bunny strips it after redeploy, add an Edge Rule setting Permissions-Policy at the CDN (zone 6292730)

findings.title: i18n-language cookie sent without Secure flag on app.jadawl.site

web-frontend/config/nuxt.config.base.ts — @nuxtjs/i18n detectBrowserLanguage defaults cookieSecure to false
findings.fix: added cookieSecure: true to detectBrowserLanguage (logged in PATCHES.md). Cookie is non-sensitive (locale); HttpOnly stays off so client JS can read it.
findings.verify: after deploy: curl -sI https://app.jadawl.site | grep -i set-cookie

findings.title: Dev-only lockfiles carry vulnerable packages (not shipped in the production image)
evidence: e2e-tests/yarn.lock: axios 1.15.0 (7 HIGH), playwright 1.48.0, nanoid, postcss
integrations/zapier/yarn.lock: form-data 4.0.0 CVE-2025-7783 (CRITICAL), node-fetch, semver, lodash
backend/email_compiler/yarn.lock: 24 vulns (minimatch, brace-expansion, lodash, picomatch)
findings.fix: Run `yarn install && yarn upgrade` refreshes in e2e-tests/, integrations/zapier/, backend/email_compiler/ and commit updated lockfiles. None of these ship in the published image, so practical risk is developer-machine only.

findings.title: web-frontend/yarn.lock: brace-expansion 1.1.18/2.1.4/5.0.9 — CVE-2026-102276/102278 (HIGH, ReDoS in build-time tooling)
evidence: web-frontend/yarn.lock: 6 HIGH entries, all brace-expansion
findings.fix: Add a resolution pin in web-frontend/package.json ("brace-expansion": "^5.0.10" respecting existing ranges) or run yarn dedupe; build-time only, low practical risk.

findings.title: Containers/ Dockerfiles run as root; ':latest' base tags; bare 'RUN <pkg> update'
evidence: trivy: DS-0002 in Dockerfile, Caddy.Dockerfile, deploy/all-in-one/Dockerfile, deploy/apache/recommended/Dockerfile, embeddings/Dockerfile; DS-0001 ':latest' in deploy/all-in-one; DS-0017 RUN update alone
findings.fix: Most are inherited from upstream base images (root Dockerfile is a pull-through pin). For deploy/all-in-one, pin base images by digest (pattern already used by root Dockerfile) and add USER where feasible. Low urgency: the CranL deployment image is pinned by digest.

findings.title: GitHub Actions pinned to mutable version tags (@v3/@v4/@v6/@v7) not commit SHAs
evidence: .github/workflows/jadawel-ci.yml:41,88,122,... publish-image.yml:49,59,62 (20 hits, semgrep github-actions-mutable-action-tag)
findings.fix: Pin third-party actions (astral-sh/setup-uv, extractions/setup-just, docker/*, actions/*) to full commit SHAs with a version comment. Repo is private which lowers supply-chain exposure.

findings.title: website/support.js postMessage: wildcard target origin and unvalidated incoming messages
evidence: website/support.js:1391,1862 (wildcard-postmessage-configuration) — outgoing messages carry only __dc_design_mode / __dc_booted state, no secrets
website/support.js:1411 — listener accepts only __dc_theme and __dc_probe types (CSS theme toggling), limiting impact
findings.fix: Third-party generated bundle (dc-runtime). If modifiable upstream, restrict the postMessage target origin to the known embed parent; incoming handler impact is bounded to theme toggling. Acceptable residual risk if the bundle is vendor-managed.

findings.title: JWT access token passed in WebSocket URL query string (?jwt_token=...)
evidence: web-frontend/modules/core/plugins/realTimeHandler.js:65-67 — new WebSocket(`${url}?jwt_token=${token}`)
findings.fix: URL query strings are captured in server access logs, proxy/CDN logs, and can leak via Referer on redirects. Tokens are short-lived access JWTs which bounds the replay window. Inherited from upstream Baserow's Django Channels design; fixing it properly requires a WS auth-ticket or Sec-WebSocket-Protocol mechanism in core (backend ASGI middleware + this plugin), so it is a core-file change to plan deliberately rather than patch. Mitigations to prefer in the meantime: keep access-token lifetime short, and if the edge proxy (Caddy) logs query strings, consider disabling that for /ws/.
findings.verify: code review of new WS handshake; grep access logs for jwt_token

findings.title: Dashboard share password has no minimum length (hashed correctly with Django hashers)
evidence: backend/src/arabase/dashboard/share/models.py:56-62 uses make_password/check_password (good); handler.set_password accepts any non-empty string
findings.fix: Optionally enforce a minimum length (e.g. 6-8 chars) in handler.set_password and surface it in the share form. Guesses already share JADAWEL_DASHBOARD_AUTH_RATE limiting.

findings.title: Markdown v-html sinks use markdown-it with html:false — safe today, fragile later
evidence: web-frontend/modules/core/components/MarkdownIt.vue:7 v-html with new Markdown() (html disabled by default)

web-frontend/modules/database/components/view/grid/fields/GridViewFieldRichText.vue:18 (+ Functional/RowCard variants) — parseMarkdown() explicitly sets { html: false }, links get rel=noopener noreferrer nofollow
findings.fix: Make new Markdown({ html: false }) explicit in MarkdownIt.vue so enabling raw HTML later is a deliberate, reviewed change; consider DOMPurify as defense-in-depth on parseMarkdown output.
